title: Beginner Finger Stretch Exercise for Guitar: Four-Finger Fretting and Down-Picking
summary: This video presents a beginner-friendly finger-stretching drill for guitar, delivered by JustinGuitar. The instructor emphasizes slow, controlled stretching rather than speed, framing the exercise as a cross-string fretting pattern that develops finger independence, reach, and precision. The core drill starts with the first finger on the 5th fret of the thickest string and adds the 2nd, 3rd, and little finger in sequence, then moves the pattern across to the 5th string and repeats. Alongside the left-hand work, the video introduces an all-down-picks right-hand approach and discusses anchoring the little finger while picking, with guidance on keeping fingers close to the frets and maintaining a palm alignment parallel to the fretboard. The instructor notes common anatomical variations (e.g., 2nd/3rd fingers tending to stay together; 1st/little finger splaying) and stresses a forgiving, patient approach for beginners. A practical practice prescription is given: about two minutes per day for one to two weeks, gradually increasing difficulty by shifting closer to the nut as comfort grows. The lesson also covers left-handed demonstrations, addressing common early struggles, and ends with encouragement and a reminder that progress comes with consistent, mindful practice across weeks.
